name: Vilnius International Airport
before:
Lithuania's largest airport, 5.9 km south of central Vilnius, carrying around 5 million passengers a year on a single runway. It is second busiest in the Baltic states after Riga, and a base for airBaltic, Ryanair and Wizz Air.

The name changed recently and only for a while. From 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2029 it is officially Vilnius Čiurlionis International Airport, in honour of the composer and painter Mikalojus Konstantinas Čiurlionis. That is a fixed-term renaming, so both names will be in circulation and the old one returns at the end of the decade.

The terminal is worth a look on arrival. The current building was built between 1949 and 1954 in standard Soviet airport style, decorated outside with sculptures of soldiers, workers and aviators, and inside with wreaths, bay leaves and stars. Until the early 1990s it carried the hammer and sickle too. A new departures terminal was added in 1993 and the old building now handles arrivals only.
after:
Lithuania's largest airport, 5.9 km south of central Vilnius, with a single runway and more than 5.1 million passengers in 2025, second only to Riga among Baltic airports. Ryanair and Wizz Air have bases here, and airBaltic also flies from Vilnius.

In 2025 it was given the symbolic name Vilnius Čiurlionis Airport, after the composer and painter Mikalojus Konstantinas Čiurlionis. Its code is still VNO.

A new departure terminal opened in February 2025. The older terminals are being rebuilt, and a new arrivals terminal is due by late 2028.

Since late 2025, smuggling balloons from Belarus have repeatedly forced the airport to halt flights, sometimes overnight. Some flights have been diverted to Kaunas.

claims.claim: given a symbolic name, Vilnius Čiurlionis Airport, in 2025
claims.inAfter: In 2025 it was given the symbolic name Vilnius Čiurlionis Airport
claims.note: Was "From 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2029 it is officially Vilnius Čiurlionis International Airport". The Lithuanian Government Office, which ran the Čiurlionis 150 programme, calls it a symbolic naming made as part of the 2025 anniversary programme, and gives no end date. Wikipedia says "renamed" and gives 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2029; the Lithuanian Wikipedia cites a Government news item for it (lrv.lt, headline "Vilniaus oro uostas 2025 metus pasitinka su simboliniu vardu", that is, greets 2025 with a symbolic name), but lrv.lt and the operator's sites answer with a Cloudflare bot check. So the text uses the Government's word, symbolic, and drops "officially" and the dates. The same release appears on Delfi (23 February 2026).

claims.claim: since late 2025 smuggling balloons from Belarus have repeatedly halted flights
claims.inAfter: Since late 2025, smuggling balloons from Belarus have repeatedly forced the airport to halt flights
claims.note: Added because it will catch a traveller out and the September text missed it (current Wikipedia has it for 2025). Lithuanian Airports counts more than 300 flights and about 47,000 passengers disrupted in 2025 and nearly 60 hours of closures (LRT, 13 May 2026); LRT counts about ten disruptions in 2026 so far, the latest overnight on 21 to 22 September 2026. The Government declared a national emergency at the end of 2025. Flag for the owner, as a new fact rather than a replacement.
